newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Irish PM sees Sweden qualifying for EMU in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Irish PM sees Sweden qualifying for EMU in 1999.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton on Tuesday said it was his personal opinion Sweden could fulfil the criteria to join Europe's Economic and Monetary Union in 1999 without now linking the crown to the ERM.

Asked at a news conference whether Sweden could do so without first entering the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), Bruton said: "I would imagine without any authority of office that if Sweden wanted to enter the euro in 1998, and economic fundamentals are on track, I don't think there would be a problem."
Bruton, who currently hold the rotating presidency of the European Union, was in Sweden to prepare for an economic union summit in Dublin in December.
He emphasised that his views were those of "an intelligent layman".
He said he was unwilling to cast himself forward and preempt any decision by the EU council of ministers on EMU membership in 1998.
